messages:
alex_support: Hey team — Acme reporting mid-stream 429s on SSE today, partial output (stream stops with error) and their billing shows token counts higher than what they received. Customer says it started after they rotated tokens. Full notes below.

jess_ops: Oof. Can you paste the minimal repro + headers they used?

alex_support: They used our SSE endpoint with Authorization: Bearer <rotated-token>. Repro curl they ran:
```
curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>\" \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=redwood-lite\" -d '\"prompt: hi\"'
```
They see data for ~30s then the stream returns a 429 and closes. On our logs the request id is rwd-req-9a7c.

mike_engineer: Are they doing client-side reconnects with a new token mid-stream? That can cause attribution issues. Do we have connection/session id?

alex_support: Customer says they rotate the token at 25s and the client code does a reconnect attempt using the new token. They provided our logs: 
```
[2024-06-12T15:02:11Z] rwd-req-9a7c stream chunk seq=18
[2024-06-12T15:02:36Z] rwd-req-9a7c 429 rate_limit mid-stream reason=token_quota_exhausted
[2024-06-12T15:02:37Z] conn=conn-42 reconnect attempt token=<rotated> -> new-req-id rwd-req-9a7d
```
Billing ledger shows a charge 2x the expected tokens: they were charged for both rwd-req-9a7c and rwd-req-9a7d but the client only stitched partial output from the first.

kevin_dev: That log pattern screams dual attribution. If the original connection hits a 429 before client reconnect succeeds, our accounting may record consumed tokens for both the original and the reconnect but deliver only the final partial output. We have a known edge case: token rotation + reconnect can create overlapping sessions without proper attribution.

mike_engineer: Repro steps we should try: 1) open SSE stream w/ token A, stream ~25s, 2) rotate token on client, force reconnect with token B mid-stream, 3) cross-check our request ids and ledger entries. Can someone run this in staging with a small model?

jess_ops: I can run it now in staging. Any headers/flags to add to surface more debug?

mike_engineer: Set X-Client-Session: <uuid> on both attempts; that'll help correlate. Also enable debug-log: X-Debug-Mode: true to include per-chunk accounting in logs.

[jess_ops later]: Ran repro in staging. Results: original req rwd-stg-77 returned a 429 at chunk 16, client did reconnect with token B -> new req rwd-stg-78. Ledger shows both requests recorded ~same token batch. Attaching condensed log: 
```
rwd-stg-77 seq=1..16 tokens=320 status=429
rwd-stg-78 seq=17..40 tokens=640 status=200
ledger: rwd-stg-77 charged tokens=320, rwd-stg-78 charged tokens=640, total=960
client stitched only seq=1..40 but customer only expected ~640 tokens on invoice (they paid for 960).
```

sara_billing: I'll open an accounting review. Do we have the customer account id and invoice?

alex_support: AcmeCorp acct acme-1122, invoice INV-2024-06-15. They're asking for a temporary credit while we investigate.

billing-bot: A billing case has been created: CASE-8934 for acme-1122 referencing rwd-req-9a7c/rwd-req-9a7d.

kevin_dev: Potential short-term mitigation: recommend clients avoid token rotation mid-active stream. If rotation is necessary, do it between sessions, not while stream is open. We can also add server-side affinity by session header so reconnects that include prior session id get merged for accounting.

mike_engineer: Longer term fix: ensure atomic accounting for stream sessions. If a reconnect occurs within a grace window (<5s) and includes an X-Client-Session matching an earlier stream, attribute consumption to a single session id and avoid double-charge. Make ticket.

alex_support: Can you create the engineering ticket and include staging repro logs? Customer wants ETA for fix and a credit meanwhile.

mike_engineer: Creating ticket INFRA-2145: \"stream accounting: merge mid-stream reconnects with token rotation\". Assigning to kevin_dev, priority P2. ETA for mitigation patch to staging: 3 business days.

kevin_dev: I'll spike a patch today to 1) treat X-Client-Session as the primary session key for accounting, 2) add a 10s dedupe window for near-simultaneous reqs. If that looks good we'll ship to canary.

sara_billing: We can issue a one-time credit for INV-2024-06-15 for acme-1122 pending root cause. I'll coordinate with finance.

alex_support: Thanks. I'll update the customer: temporary credit + we're working on a server change to avoid double-charge when they reconnect after token rotation. Also recommending client-side guidance: rotate tokens outside active streams or include same X-Client-Session so we can merge.

mike_engineer: FYI: we should also log the Authorization token id (redacted) to help link token rotations to ledger entries for audits. Add to ticket.

deploybot: INFRA-2145 created and linked to canary pipeline.

alex_support: Ok closing from support for now, will reopen if customer sees further unexpected charges. :thumbsup:
